name: rsi3 washout uptrend
note: Stop-loss and liquidation flow makes a 3-bar washout overshoot in an uptrend; forced sellers pay the spread and liquidity providers earn the rebound.

name: rsi3 spike downtrend
note: Breakout chasers and shorts covering into a 3-bar spike inside a downtrend overpay for immediacy; trend-side sellers fade the overshoot.

name: below vwap reversion
note: Institutional execution algos benchmark to VWAP and buy below it; retail sellers dumping under VWAP transact worse than the benchmark and get absorbed.

name: above vwap reversion
note: Sell-side benchmark algos work orders above VWAP; late buyers paying above the volume-weighted average face steady supply and lose to reversion.

name: trend state hold
note: Large orders are sliced over hours or days, so a confirmed uptrend state keeps receiving parent-order flow; those who sold early are forced to chase or stay short.

name: trend state hold short
note: Sliced institutional selling persists through a confirmed downtrend state; buyers of the dip are on the wrong side of an unfinished parent order.

name: sharp 3bar drop uptrend
note: A fast 3-bar drop in an uptrend is mostly liquidity-driven selling (stops, liquidations); it carries no new information so price mean-reverts once sellers are exhausted.

name: sharp 3bar pop downtrend
note: A fast 3-bar rally in a downtrend is mostly short-covering and momentum chasing; it carries no new information and fades once the forced buyers are done.

name: persistent range floor
note: Two consecutive bars pinned at the bottom of the range mean sellers have been paying up for immediacy; the market maker taking the other side collects reversion as the flow dries up.

name: persistent range ceiling
note: Two consecutive bars pinned at the top of the range mean buyers have been paying up for immediacy; passive sellers collect reversion as that flow dries up.

name: squeeze release up
note: Range sellers who sold the narrowing squeeze are short with tight stops; when the envelope expands upward their stops become forced buying.

name: squeeze release down
note: Range buyers who bought the narrowing squeeze have tight stops; when the envelope expands downward their stops become forced selling.

name: capitulation spike buy
note: A spike down is stop-run and liquidation flow, not informed selling; forced sellers exit at the worst price and buyers of the wick are paid by the rebound.

name: blowoff spike sell
note: A spike up is short-squeeze and FOMO buying that overshoots fair value; forced buyers pay the top and sellers of the wick are paid as it retraces.

name: swing buy in uptrend
note: A swing low inside an uptrend marks where trapped shorts and early sellers are forced to cover or accept a loss as the higher low holds.

name: swing sell in downtrend
note: A swing high inside a downtrend marks where trapped longs and dip-buyers are forced to sell or accept a loss as the lower high holds.

name: smc long with trend
note: Sell stops clustered under obvious lows get swept by large players who then buy the liquidity; the stopped-out retail traders are the forced counterparties.

name: smc short with trend
note: Buy stops clustered above obvious highs get swept by large players who then sell the liquidity; the stopped-out retail shorts are the forced counterparties.

name: uptrend pullback
note: Trend-following holders add on dips while short-term sellers in an established uptrend buy back at the trend line to cover, so the dip sellers are the losers.

name: downtrend rally fade
note: Dip buyers who catch a bounce inside an established downtrend get trapped when trend sellers reload and the bounce stalls.

name: quiet uptrend drift
note: Range sellers and vol sellers sit short into quiet uptrends and must cover when volatility re-expands, so their stops feed the move.

name: demand bull with trend
note: Exhausted sellers at a demand pivot inside an uptrend are running out of inventory; late shorts must cover into the trend.

name: demand bear with trend
note: Buyers who step in at a supply pivot inside a downtrend are counter-trend and get squeezed out as the trend resumes.

name: boom long in uptrend
note: Breakout sellers and range fadeurs are wrong-footed by a boom bar with trend support and cover with stops above the range.

name: boom short in downtrend
note: Dip buyers and range fadeurs are caught by a downward boom bar in a downtrend and have to sell stops below the range.

name: neural long not stretched
note: Model signal only when price is not yet extended, so it is not buying from exhausted late buyers; the losers are early shorts who have not covered.

name: neural short not stretched
note: Model signal only when price is not already washed out, so the counterparty is late dip buyers rather than capitulated sellers.

name: arbm long
note: Signal fires often, so it tests mostly whether cross-bar imbalance flow persists; the losers are passive sellers being lifted through the spread.

name: arbm short
note: Mirror of the long signal: passive buyers are hit through the bid by persistent imbalance flow.

name: fade blowoff spike
note: Spike buyers are stop-outs of shorts and breakout chasers; once that forced demand is exhausted, price reverts and chasers hold losses.

name: buy panic in uptrend
note: Panic sellers and stopped-out longs create a one-off downward spike inside an uptrend; the forced selling is finished and price recovers.

name: deep below vwap reversion
note: Sellers who push far under volume-weighted average price are paying worse than the average participant, and execution algos benchmarked to VWAP buy back toward it.

name: far above vwap reversion
note: Buyers paying far above VWAP are chasing; VWAP-benchmarked execution algos sell into strength and pull price back to average.

name: sustained above vwap
note: Large orders being worked to a VWAP benchmark are buying persistently through the day; sellers who fade it are absorbing a slow institutional bid.

name: sustained below vwap
note: Institutional sell programs are worked persistently below VWAP; buyers trying to catch the bottom are absorbing a slow supply that cannot be hidden.

name: low dispersion upside
note: Sellers of options-like range and mean-reversion traders lean short in low dispersion and are forced to buy back when the range breaks upward.

name: vol surge overbought fade
note: Buyers arriving in a volatility surge at overbought levels are momentum chasers with poor entries; the surge ends when their buying is used up.

name: vol surge oversold capitulation
note: Forced sellers hit stops and margin calls in a volatile flush; once their liquidation is done, supply disappears and price bounces.

name: trend dip under fast average
note: Weak longs and short-term traders sell the dip below the fast average in an intact uptrend, while trend followers and dip buyers absorb that selling.

name: bear-rally fade rsi55
note: Dip-buyers who bought a downtrend rally are trapped under the falling trend average; when the bounce stalls they capitulate, giving sellers an exit into their forced stop-outs.

name: downtrend overbought fade
note: Buyers who push momentum overbought while the higher-timeframe trend is down are counter-trend and get run over when trend sellers resume.

name: uptrend flush buy
note: Panic sellers and leveraged longs forced out by margin calls at a short-term flush low in an uptrend sell at the worst price; the forced flow is exhausted quickly.

name: uptrend pullback rsi7
note: Short-term sellers into an intact uptrend are profit-takers and weak hands with stops above; institutional trend allocators buy the dip and absorb their supply.

name: downtrend pullback rsi7
note: Counter-trend buyers in a downtrend have to exit into resistance; trend followers add short into the bounce and overwhelm them.

name: vol-expansion dip in uptrend
note: A volatility spike down inside an uptrend is forced deleveraging and stop-run flow; those sellers do not choose the price and liquidity providers get paid to take the other side.

name: vol-spike overbought fade
note: Overbought during a volatility burst is usually short-squeeze or FOMO buying; squeezed shorts have finished covering and late chasers are left holding the top.

name: established uptrend wpr dip
note: In a persistent uptrend, short-term sellers are impatient scalpers fighting trend allocators who buy every dip and are not price-sensitive.

name: established downtrend wpr pop
note: In a persistent downtrend, bounce buyers are early bottom-callers whose stops sit just below and feed the next leg down.

name: deep oversold above ema50
note: A very fast drop that leaves price still above the medium trend is a liquidity gap from stop-driven sellers, and it tends to be refilled by patient bid.

name: deep overbought below ema50
note: A fast rally that leaves price still under the medium trend is short-covering and stop-driven buying; once it ends there is no natural buyer left.

name: mature uptrend healthy momentum
note: Slow-moving allocators and hedgers scale into trends gradually over days, so a mature trend with healthy but not stretched momentum still has unfilled buy orders behind it.

name: mature downtrend healthy momentum
note: Gradual de-risking by slow institutional holders in a downtrend spreads supply over many bars, so a non-oversold downtrend still has unfilled sell orders behind it.

name: two-bar dip in sustained uptrend
note: Two consecutive bars of selling in a ten-bar uptrend is mostly intraday profit-taking by day traders; trend holders do not sell, so the dip lacks follow-through.

name: two-bar pop in sustained downtrend
note: Two bars of buying in a ten-bar downtrend is short-term bounce chasing; trend sellers do not cover, so the pop lacks follow-through and reverses.

name: persistent capitulation in uptrend
note: Three bars pinned at the bottom of the range means forced sellers have been hitting bids with no relief; the supply is nearly spent and holders who did not sell are strong.

name: persistent squeeze in downtrend
note: Three bars pinned at the top of the range in a downtrend is forced short covering; when the shorts are all covered the buying disappears.

name: high-vol dip above trend
note: When volatility is elevated and momentum is washed out while price is still above trend, sellers are reacting to noise or margin pressure rather than a regime change.

name: downtrend continuation not oversold
note: Holders of losing longs in a downtrend sell into every leg down (disposition effect delays their capitulation), so momentum down with room left before oversold keeps getting fed.

name: uptrend continuation not overbought
note: Short sellers fighting an uptrend must cover into strength when losses hit their limits, and under-invested managers chase performance, so up-momentum with room left keeps getting bought.

name: below-vwap uptrend reversion
note: Volume-weighted average price is the benchmark for execution desks; buyers with VWAP mandates step in when price sits persistently below it, in an uptrend, so weak sellers get absorbed.

name: short rally in downtrend rsi14
note: Counter-trend dip buyers and short-covering push price up inside a downtrend. Trend holders sell into it, and the late buyers are stuck with losses they cannot exit without pushing price back down.

name: short wpr5 top of range in downtrend
note: Buying at the top of a 5-bar range in a down-trending market is mostly stop-run and short-covering flow. Once the covering is done nobody is left to hold price up, and those buyers lose.

name: short wpr14 top of range below sma100
note: Late buyers near the 14-bar high while the medium trend is down are fading the trend. Holders trapped underwater use the bounce to get out and cap the move.

name: short sharp 3-bar pop in downtrend
note: A fast pop in a downtrend is typically a liquidity vacuum or short squeeze. Once the forced buyers are done, price falls back, and whoever bought the pop pays for it.

name: short upward spike in downtrend
note: An upward spike inside a downtrend is stop-triggered buying by shorts who got squeezed. That flow is one-off and forced, with no lasting demand behind it, so the spike unwinds.

name: short 20-bar breakdown in downtrend
note: Longs with stops resting under the recent low are forced sellers when it breaks. Their market-order exits push price further down, and they cannot wait because their stops trigger automatically.

name: short pullback in established downtrend
note: After ten bars of downtrend, a bounce to the top of the 7-bar range draws in dip buyers who are fighting the trend. Trapped longs sell into that strength.

name: long rsi14 reclaim 50 in uptrend
note: When a pullback ends inside an uptrend, shorts who sold the dip are underwater and must cover. Their forced buying adds to the resumption.

name: short rsi14 lose 50 in downtrend
note: When a bounce fails in a downtrend, dip buyers are underwater and their stops trigger. Their forced selling adds to the resumption of the decline.

name: long vwap50 reclaim in uptrend
note: Sellers who pushed price under the volume-weighted average are underwater once price reclaims it. Their covering, plus benchmark-anchored buyers, supports the move.

name: short vwap50 loss in downtrend
note: Buyers who bought above the volume-weighted average are underwater when price loses it. Their stops and benchmark-anchored sellers add supply, and they cannot avoid exiting.

name: long exit from oversold in uptrend
note: Sellers who pushed price to the bottom of its range in an uptrend are the weak hands. When price turns back up, they buy to cover and chase, which extends the rebound.

name: short exit from overbought in downtrend
note: Buyers who pushed price to the top of its range in a downtrend are the weak hands. When price turns down, they sell to cut losses and the decline extends.

name: long volatility burst up in uptrend
note: Volatility expansion with price at the top of its range forces short sellers and option hedgers to buy back. They must cover regardless of price because their risk limits are hit.

name: short volatility burst down in downtrend
note: Volatility expansion with price at the bottom of its range triggers stops and margin-driven liquidations of longs. They must sell into a falling market and cannot wait for a bounce.

name: short volatile bounce below ema200
note: A bounce with rising volatility below the long-term average is usually a squeeze of shorts, not new demand. When forced covering ends, sellers of the larger downtrend return.

name: downtrend spike sell
note: Dip-buyers who bought a sharp bounce inside a downtrend are trapped as sellers resume. They own inventory above the trend and their stops sit just under the bounce low, so they sell into the turn.

name: bear rally exhaustion
note: Short-covering rallies in a bear regime run out of forced buyers. Shorts who covered are done, and the underlying trend sellers such as hedgers and trend funds add supply again.

name: bear pullback rally sell
note: Counter-trend buyers lift price above the fast average inside a downtrend. Their conviction is weak and trend-following supply sits overhead, so the bounce fades.

name: 50-bar breakdown in bear trend
note: A break of a 50-bar floor in a downtrend triggers stops of range-bound longs and dip-buyers who have no exit except selling. That flow adds to trend supply.

name: fast drop in uptrend
note: Panic sellers and stop-outs in an uptrend hit the bid with a fast drop. Market makers absorb that flow at a discount and revert it once the forced selling ends.

name: pullback turn in uptrend
note: Short-term sellers who pushed price under the fast average for 4 bars have no thesis against the larger uptrend. When the drop stalls, they cover into buyers who are waiting.

name: calm uptrend drift
note: When volatility is low in an uptrend, option sellers and carry traders are comfortable and keep supplying stable bids. Sellers who fade calm markets are slow to adjust, so upward drift continues.

name: calm downtrend drift
note: A quiet downtrend has steady seller flow, for example from hedgers and fund rebalancing. Dip-buyers keep showing up early and get run over slowly, so price grinds lower.

name: quiet dip in up-cross
note: In a quiet market with a fresh up-trend, a dip below the fast average is shallow profit-taking. Momentum buyers who missed the first leg use these dips to enter.

name: above-vwap pullback
note: Sellers pressing below fair value in a session above VWAP are short-term flippers. Institutions benchmarked to VWAP buy dips toward it, and they absorb the flippers.

name: below-vwap bounce sell
note: Buyers lifting price toward VWAP after a stretch below it are holding losing inventory. Institutions who need to sell benchmarked to VWAP unload into the bounce.

name: sustained dip in bull
note: Extended weakness in the range inside a rising market squeezes out weak longs through forced margin calls. Once they are gone, the longer-term holders face no more supply.

name: bear momentum roll-over
note: In a bear regime, upward momentum fading through +50bp means squeezed shorts have finished covering. The supply of forced buyers is spent and trend sellers resume.

name: bear acceleration
note: When 10-bar momentum falls through -50bp, longs who held for a bounce hit their loss limits. Their forced selling accelerates the fall before new buyers can arrive.

name: bull dip recovery
note: In an uptrend, RSI recovering from the 30s marks the end of a shakeout. Weak longs have already sold and sidelined buyers return to a supply-thin market.

name: bear rally rollover
note: In a downtrend, RSI turning down from the 60s marks the end of a short-covering bounce. The shorts who covered are done and the buyers left are late and underwater.

name: quiet downtrend resolution
note: A compressed range under falling averages leaves the trapped longs at breakeven. When they finally sell, volatility expands to the downside as the stops trigger together.

name: persistent bull strength
note: Price holding the top of a 50-bar range means shorts are underwater and forced to buy back. Their covering keeps supporting price while trend funds add.

name: persistent bear weakness
note: Price pinned at the bottom of a 50-bar range in a downtrend means longs are underwater and trapped. Their margin calls and loss limits keep producing supply.

name: bear rally fade rsi60
note: In a downtrend, dip-buyers who chase a bounce to RSI 60 are late; trend sellers and hedgers resume supply and those late longs are forced out at a loss.

name: downtrend wpr5 top
note: Short-covering spikes to the top of a 5-bar range inside a downtrend are liquidity bounces; the shorts who covered are not replaced by real buyers and the bid fades.

name: bear rsi3 spike fade
note: Sharp 3-bar squeezes in a bear regime are forced short covering; once stops are exhausted, the buyers are gone and price mean-reverts to the trend.

name: below ema50 rsi5 overbought
note: Retail bottom-pickers buy the first sharp bounce under the 50 average; they hold no edge and their stops feed trend sellers.

name: bear roc5 pop fade
note: Fast pops against a falling long-term trend are stop-run short squeezes; the squeezed shorts are done buying and no natural buyer follows.

name: short downtrend pullback rsi55
note: Pullbacks in a short-term downtrend attract early reversal buyers; trapped longs must sell when the trend resumes and their losses grow.

name: uptrend low sweep buy
note: Breaks of the 20-bar low inside an uptrend are mostly stop-hunts; breakout sellers and stop-loss orders are the flow, and once filled there is no more supply.

name: downtrend high sweep sell
note: Breakout buyers above the 20-bar high in a bear trend are trapped; their stops and the trend sellers supply the move back down.

name: downtrend breakdown continue
note: Breakdowns in a downtrend trigger stop-loss orders from longs and sell-stop entries from trend followers, which forces sequential selling that cannot be avoided.

name: vol bear top of range
note: In a volatile downtrend, a run to the top of the 10-bar range is a squeeze on forced short covering; trapped late buyers get sold into.

name: bear relief top hold
note: A sustained 4-bar hold near the top of a 30-bar range in a bear regime is a relief rally that buyers overpay for; hedgers reload shorts there.

name: sustained strength uptrend
note: Prolonged closes near the top of the range in an uptrend reflect persistent institutional accumulation; shorts who fade it are forced to cover as it grinds higher.

name: uptrend 10-bar low flush
note: Flushes to a 10-bar low inside an established uptrend are forced liquidations of leveraged late longs and stop orders; after they clear, trend buyers take the other side.

name: uptrend panic drop
note: Sharp drops during a volatility burst in an uptrend are panic selling and margin-call liquidations that pay a premium for immediacy; liquidity providers who take the other side earn it.

name: downtrend range-top short
note: Dip buyers in a downtrend push to the top of the range. Trapped longs sell into that strength to break even, which caps the move.

name: weak-trend bounce short
note: Bounce buyers meet supply from holders underwater since the last leg down. Those holders sell at break-even and cannot wait for more.

name: short low break in downtrend
note: In an established downtrend, stops of late dip buyers sit just under recent lows. Breaking those lows triggers forced selling.

name: fade rally below trend
note: Short covering creates a quick rally against the main trend. Once the covering ends there are no natural buyers left, so price slides back.

name: extreme overbought fade
note: Momentum chasers buy after a near-vertical run and have no plan for a pullback. Liquidity providers who sold to them take profits, and the run stalls.

name: quiet-range breakout long
note: Range sellers and short-vol positions sit near the top of a quiet range. Their stops are hit on a break and they must buy back.

name: quiet-range breakdown short
note: Range buyers who leaned on the bottom of a quiet range have their stops clustered under it. A break forces them to sell into a market with thin support.

name: capitulation long
note: Forced sellers (margin calls, stop-outs) dump at any price after a new 50-bar low. Once they are done the price snaps back toward where it was.

name: blow-off short
note: Late breakout buyers and short-squeezed shorts drive a new high on forced buying. When the squeeze is over the buying vanishes.

name: panic drop long
note: A fast drop is mostly stop-outs and liquidations, not new information. Whoever sold at the low was forced to, and the price tends to recover.

name: spike-up short
note: A fast rise is mostly forced short covering and FOMO buying. Once those buyers are used up there is no one left to push it higher.

name: pullback recovery long
note: Trend-following buyers wait for price to reclaim the medium average in an uptrend. Shorts who sold the dip are squeezed out at that same level.

name: sustained strength long
note: Sustained strength means shorts and under-invested funds keep having to chase. Their buying is forced by tracking and risk limits, and it spreads over many bars.

name: above-VWAP trend long
note: Execution algorithms benchmarked to VWAP keep buying dips to VWAP during an uptrend. Sellers there are the ones who sold too early.

name: spike-down reversal long
note: A sudden downward spike is largely stop-runs and forced liquidation with no follow-through. Sellers at the low were forced, so price recovers once they are done.

name: spike-up reversal short
note: An upward spike against the trend is short covering and stop-runs. When the forced buyers are done, price falls back with the trend.

name: demand zone long
note: Bulls who defend a demand zone must add or lose their earlier buys. Shorts entering into that zone are stopped out above VWAP.

name: downtrend top of 5-bar range
note: Buying at the top of a tiny range under a falling trend is a late bounce chase. Trend sellers wait for exactly that.

name: rsi high under ema100
note: An RSI of 65 under the 100 average means a large counter-trend rally. Holders from higher levels use it to exit at a better price, which caps the move.

name: downtrend breakdown
note: A new 20-bar low under the 200 average triggers stops of dip buyers and range longs. Their forced selling pushes the price further down.

name: volatile bounce sold
note: A bounce inside a downtrend during high volatility is often forced buying from shorts covering. Once the cover ends, the trend resumes.

name: uptrend exhaustion fade
note: An RSI above 78 marks a stretched move where the last buyers are chasing. Earlier buyers take profit into that demand. The wide stop allows for trend persistence.

name: capitulation bounce
note: An RSI below 20 means forced sellers: margin calls and stop-outs, whose selling is not price-driven. When that ends, the price snaps back.

name: uptrend dip to range low
note: A dip to the bottom of the range in an uptrend is shakeout selling by weak hands and stop-runs. Trend holders and dip buyers absorb it.

name: sharp drop in uptrend
note: A drop of 2% or more in 20 bars inside an uptrend is panic or forced liquidation. It is not a change in the underlying trend, and the sellers cannot keep selling.

name: persistent oversold in uptrend
note: Two bars of oversold RSI while the price holds above the 50 average shows sustained selling that fails to break support. The sellers run out and the trend buyers return.

name: downtrend fast pop
note: A quick pop in a downtrend pulls in momentum buyers and short covering. The larger trend holders sell into it and the move reverses.

name: dip above long vwap
note: The price holds above long-run average cost, so most holders are in profit. A dip to the bottom of the range is impatient selling, and holders in profit do not sell into it.

name: rally below long vwap
note: The price sits below long-run average cost, so most holders are underwater. A rally to the top of the range gives them a chance to exit at breakeven, which caps the move.

name: downtrend rally fade
note: In a downtrend, late buyers chase bounces into overhead supply. Trapped longs from higher up sell into strength, and the chasers have no exit once the bounce fails.

name: bear spike-up fade
note: A sudden upward spike against a falling trend is usually stop-running of shorts or a market order chasing thin depth. Once the forced buyers finish, price returns to where the flow was.

name: bear demand signal
note: When the demand signal turns bearish under the 100-bar average, there are fewer buyers than resting sellers. Longs holding from higher up cannot exit without pushing price lower.

name: neural short not oversold
note: Shorting only when price is not already oversold avoids selling into exhausted sellers. The counterparty is late longs who still have room to lose.

name: arbm short in downtrend
note: Short-side mean-reversion signal when the larger trend is down. Buyers fading the decline are the counterparty and get run over when the trend continues.

name: short-term bear bounce top
note: Fast trend is down and price has bounced to the top of a 7-bar range. Buyers there are betting on a reversal that the trend does not support, and they are exposed to the next leg down.

name: vol expansion bear bounce
note: In an expanding-volatility downtrend, bounces are short-covering, not new demand. Shorts covering are forced buyers and they stop once flat.

name: stretched above vwap
note: Price well above volume-weighted average with high RSI means buyers are paying more than the average participant. Those buyers are trapped if price reverts to VWAP, which is where benchmark-driven execution tends to trade.

name: bounce rollover
note: Price has held above the fast average during a bounce and momentum then turns negative. The bounce buyers have just lost their edge and the larger trend holders are still sellers.

name: bear-market washout long
note: An extreme low in a 14-bar range under the trend line is often forced liquidation of leveraged longs. When forced sellers finish, price snaps back and the sellers have no more to sell.

name: panic rsi3 long
note: An RSI3 under 5 means several bars of one-way selling. Panic sellers are paying for immediacy and there is nobody left to keep selling at that price.

name: aligned trend pullback
note: In a fully aligned uptrend, a pullback to neutral RSI catches profit-takers and short-term sellers. They exit for reasons unrelated to the trend and the trend holders are still buying.

name: uptrend momentum resume
note: Momentum turning positive again inside an uptrend marks the end of a dip. Sellers on the dip are short-horizon traders who have to buy back or face a bigger loss.

name: uptrend spike continuation
note: A spike up inside an uptrend is often shorts being forced to cover. The covering continues as later shorts hit their stop levels, so the buyers are not done.

name: demand zone soft rsi
note: A demand zone touched while RSI is below neutral means price arrives at resting buy orders after sellers have pressed. Sellers there are late and the resting bids are patient.

name: swing buy at range low
note: A swing-low signal in the lower part of the range buys where breakdown sellers have entered. They are short at the low and get squeezed when the level holds.

name: smc long after sweep
note: Structure long after price sweeps lower is buying after sell stops were triggered. The sellers were forced by stops and stop selling once the stops are filled.

name: boom long soft rsi
note: A long signal when RSI is soft buys after sellers have already sold. Those sellers cannot sell twice, so the pressure that pushed price down is gone.

name: S bounce exhaustion in downtrend
note: Dip-buyers chase a bounce inside a downtrend. Their entry is above value, they hold losing longs with wide stops, and trend sellers refill supply into the bounce, so they get squeezed out.

name: S top of range under 200
note: Late bounce buyers pay the top of the short range in a down regime. Trapped longs from the prior drop sell into strength to break even, which caps the rally.

name: S failed breakout in downtrend
note: Breakout buyers and shorts who cover on a 10-bar high are the marginal flow. Against a falling 200 average there is no follow-through, so late breakout longs become sellers on the failure.

name: S pullback to fast EMA in downtrend
note: Counter-trend buyers step in at the fast average and are the losers. Trend followers reload shorts at the average, and the buyers' stops sit just above it and feed the drop.

name: S volatile relief rally
note: In a volatile down regime, short covering creates sharp relief rallies. Once the forced covering is done, the buyers are unforced and the price returns to the trend.

name: S cross up under 100 fades
note: Breakout-of-the-dip buyers enter when price crosses the fast average. Below the 100 average, supply from trapped longs waits overhead, so the cross is a fake signal.

name: S sharp rally in bear regime
note: Sharp rallies in a down regime are driven by short covering and FOMO buyers. Neither has fresh capital to keep buying, so the move mean-reverts.

name: S extreme overbought
note: Momentum chasers buy the last leg of a spike with market orders and pay the spread and slippage. Once they are all in, nobody is left to buy and early longs take profit into them.

name: S smart-money short with trend
note: Supply zones mark where large sellers already left unfilled orders. Retail buyers lifting into that zone are absorbed by the resting offers.

name: S bearish signal below VWAP
note: Below VWAP, everyone who bought during the session is under water. They sell on any bounce toward break-even, and the bearish signal marks the turn.

name: S persistent below VWAP
note: Persistent trading below VWAP means the buyers are all holding losses. Institutions benchmarked to VWAP keep selling at that benchmark and buyers cannot get out without selling.

name: L sustained oversold in uptrend
note: Sellers into a persistent dip inside an uptrend are panic sellers and leveraged longs forced out by margin. Their selling is exhausted after a few bars, and buyers of the trend take the other side.

name: L RSI7 recovery in uptrend
note: Forced sellers after a flush finish selling. When the fast RSI turns up from 30, short-term shorts who sold the low have to cover into an uptrend.

name: L capitulation turn below VWAP
note: Well below VWAP the marginal seller is a forced or capitulating holder. When RSI turns up from oversold, the forced flow is done, and shorts who chased the low have no cushion.

name: L fast cross in uptrend
note: A fast cross up inside an uptrend marks the end of a pullback. Shorts who sold the dip against the primary trend are forced to cover, and trend followers add to their longs.

name: L squeeze release up
note: A narrow-range period stacks short stops just above the range. On a release upward the shorts are forced to buy, and their covering is the fuel.

name: L neural long with trend
note: The model long only with the primary trend. Counter-trend sellers in an uptrend hold losing shorts with stops that must be bought back if the price keeps rising.

name: L arbm long on dip
note: The signal triggers on a dip below the fast average, where the marginal seller is a scalper taking a small profit. Larger holders do not sell at that level, so the dip is absorbed.

name: L swing low in uptrend
note: A swing low inside an uptrend is where breakdown sellers get trapped. Their shorts sit just under the low, and when price holds they must buy back.

name: downtrend spike rally fade
note: Late buyers chase a sharp bounce inside a downtrend. Trend sellers and shorts covered earlier re-enter at the top, and the chasers are trapped with stops just below.

name: bounce to range top in downtrend
note: Dip buyers who buy at the top of a 10-bar range inside a downtrend are counter-trend. Their stops are close and trend sellers keep supplying, so the bounce fails.

name: downtrend pullback to fast average
note: In an established downtrend, buyers who bought the dip back to the fast average are under water. Hedgers and trend-following sellers use that level to add, so the pullback gets sold.

name: below VWAP oversold reversion
note: Institutional executors benchmarked to VWAP must buy below it and the panic sellers who pushed price under it are exhausted. Those sellers are the ones who lose.

name: long-term uptrend deep dip
note: In a long-horizon uptrend, a sharp 7-bar washout is mostly forced selling from leveraged longs and margin calls. Once they are flushed, the structural bid returns.

name: stretched above VWAP fade
note: Breakout chasers who buy well above the volume-weighted average pay a premium to the average participant. Without new demand, VWAP-anchored sellers pull price back.

name: volatility flush new low
note: Volatility spikes with a fresh low mean stop-outs and liquidations, so panic sellers are price-insensitive. Liquidity providers then buy the overshoot from forced sellers.

name: capitulation low bounce
note: A fresh 50-bar low with deeply oversold momentum is where breakout shorts and stop-loss sellers pile in last. Once their supply is spent, nobody is left to sell.

name: blow-off top fade
note: A new 50-bar high on extreme momentum draws in FOMO breakout buyers and short-covering. Once the covering ends, the late buyers hold the top.

name: uptrend shallow pullback
note: Sellers in a pullback within an uptrend are short-term profit takers and weak hands. Trend allocators use the pullback to add, so the dip is absorbed.

name: downtrend shallow rally
note: Buyers in a rally within a downtrend are bottom-pickers and short-covers. Trend allocators sell into strength, so these buyers get run over.

name: quiet grind up
note: Low-volatility steady drift up squeezes short-sellers and under-invested managers. Their forced buying or chasing accumulates slowly, and they cannot wait for a pullback.

name: quiet grind down
note: A slow low-volatility bleed lets longs believe nothing is wrong, so they do not cut. Stops cluster below and get hit sequentially as the drift continues.

name: sustained strength above VWAP
note: Persistent buying with price above the 100-bar VWAP means large orders are being worked over many bars. Underweight benchmarked funds must keep buying, and sellers who fade get squeezed.

name: sustained weakness below VWAP
note: Persistent selling below the 100-bar VWAP means large sell programs are still working. Overweight holders are underwater on average and sell any bounce to exit.

name: pinned at range top under trend
note: Three bars pinned at the top of the range while price is under the 100-bar average is a counter-trend push. Buyers are running out of steam and are exposed to the larger trend.

name: pinned at range bottom oversold
note: Two bars pinned at the bottom of the range with weak momentum is a sell climax. Forced and panic sellers are done and there is no trend filter, so this catches the exhaustion.

name: volatile spike high fade
note: A volatility spike at a fresh short-term high means short-squeeze or stop-driven buying, not fresh demand. When the forced buyers are done, price snaps back.

name: sharp 20-bar drop bounce
note: A fast decline of 1.5% or more over 20 bars is driven by liquidation and stop cascades, not information. Sellers who exit in the panic sell at the low and are absorbed by patient buyers.

name: sharp 20-bar spike fade
note: A fast rally of 1.5% or more is often short-covering and momentum chasing. Once the squeezed shorts are gone there is no natural buyer left, and the chasers are left holding.

name: downward spike oversold buy
note: A sudden down-spike into oversold is usually a thin-book sweep that triggers stops. The stopped-out sellers are the losers and price often recovers once the sweep ends.

name: upward spike overbought fade
note: A sudden up-spike into overbought is usually a thin-book sweep that triggers short stops. The short-covering buyers are forced and temporary, so price reverts once done.

name: swing buy below VWAP
note: A swing-low buy signal below VWAP marks where a sell push has stalled at a discount. Discount-anchored sellers are done, and institutional buyers are benchmarked to buy under VWAP.

name: swing sell under trend
note: A swing-high sell signal below the 100-bar average marks a failed counter-trend rally. Buyers who bought the bounce are trapped below broken support and get squeezed out.

name: downtrend rsi bounce
note: Dip buyers and short-coverers push price up inside a downtrend; once their buying is spent, trend sellers resume and the late buyers are left holding losses they cannot exit cheaply.

name: range top in downtrend
note: Bottom-fishers buying at the top of a short range in a falling market are counter-trend and face supply from trapped holders selling into any strength.

name: pullback in established downtrend
note: Longs who bought the rebound above the fast average are underwater trend-fighters; their stops sit just above and feed the continuation move down.

name: fade up spike below trend
note: Upward spikes against the trend come from forced buyers (stopped-out shorts, market orders in thin books); after the forced flow ends there is no natural demand left to hold the price up.

name: swing sell with trend
note: Sellers at a swing high below the trend average meet buyers who are structurally late and hold no edge; the seller is with the flow, the buyer is against it.

name: vwap discount in uptrend
note: Sellers pushing price below volume-weighted average in an uptrend are short-term liquidity takers; institutional buyers benchmarked to VWAP absorb the discount and must fill their orders.

name: quiet uptrend compression
note: Short-vol sellers and range traders fade a quiet market above trend; when volatility expands they are forced to cover, and the direction of expansion usually follows the prevailing trend.

name: squeeze end above ema200
note: Range-fade sellers who sold the compressed range are caught when the envelope stops narrowing; with the long-term trend up, their forced cover pushes price further.

name: squeeze end below ema50
note: Range-fade buyers who bought the compressed range's lows are caught on release; below the trend average their stops become the fuel for the move.

name: vwap-supported calm trend
note: Steady grind above VWAP with shrinking ranges: benchmark-driven buyers keep filling slowly, and fade-sellers are repeatedly squeezed in small increments.

name: sell-off cascade continuation
note: Longs underwater below VWAP in an expanding-volatility decline face margin and stop pressure; they must sell into a falling market and that supply persists over several bars.

name: swing buy above ema100
note: Buying swing lows in an uptrend takes the other side of panicked short-term sellers who are selling the dip at the worst price.

name: smc long above ema200
note: Demand-zone retests in a long-term uptrend catch counter-trend shorts whose stops sit just below the zone and whose covering supports the bounce.

name: demand bull in dip
note: Zone support that holds while price sits in the lower half of its range takes the other side of sellers who are late and already extended.

name: neural long calm vwap
note: Signal firing in a calm market above VWAP means fade-sellers have low conviction; when volatility rises they are the ones who must cover.

name: overextended uptrend fade
note: Late momentum chasers buying after a fast run are the marginal buyers; once the initial holders take profit there is no fresh demand and the chasers become forced sellers.

name: capitulation below trend
note: Liquidation selling at the bottom of the range in a volatility spike comes from forced sellers (margin calls, stops) who are not price-sensitive; buyers on the other side collect the overshoot.
